'''''Cynanchica aristata''''', commonly known as woodruff,<ref>{{Cite web |title=woodruff (herb) |url=https://www.britannica.com/plant/woodruff-herb |access-date=13 May 2024 |website=Britannica}}</ref> is a [[deciduous]] [[species]] of perennial groundcover, and a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Rubiaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=Bojňanský |first1=Vít |title=Atlas of seeds and fruits of central and east-European flora: the Carpathian Mountains region |last2=Bojňanský |first2=Vít |last3=Fargašová |first3=Agáta |date=2007 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4020-5362-7 |location=Dordrecht London}}</ref> It is native to Morocco, Libya, Algeria, Tunisia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Greece, Bulgaria, Albania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Croatia, Italy, Austria, Switzerland, France, Spain, and Portugal.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Cynanchica aristata (L.f.) P.Caputo & Del Guacchio {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77215279-1 |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Cynanchica aristata'' appears as a long green plant, {{Convert|10-60|cm|4=0|abbr=on}} high,<ref name=":0" /> with small (1in) pale purple flowers, on long, thin, green, stems. It has thin, green, grass-like leaves. It flowers around May–June.

==Cultivation==
{{Unreferenced section|date=March 2022}}
''Cynanchica aristata'' grows best in a rock garden, trough or crevice.
